items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
6 - 10 years of related experience.
Experience using UCR financial and administrative systems.
Minimum 6 years of experience in post-award financial management within research administration, specifically in contracts and grants.
Minimum of 6 years of experience in quantitative data analysis and reporting related to post-award financial management, using spreadsheet and database applications.
Experience with research proposal preparation for submission of contract and grant proposals to federal agencies
Thorough knowledge of federal, state, and location regulations and issues related to research administration. Working knowledge of Uniform Guidance and OMB Circulars.

Department Role (DR): Leads the organization, planning, establishment and monitoring of fiscal budget control of contracts and grants administration, submissions, budgets, support documents, gifts, endowments and privately funded projects for faculty research programs. Independently guide PIs and collaborators in the preparation and submission of complex grant proposals, including development of project budgets, ensuring compliance with sponsor, department, and university requirements. Coordinate the collection of materials from all parties involved, including PIs, external collaborators, subaward organizations, and central campus offices to ensure timely submission and compliance with all requirements. (30% time)

(DR): Administers, in coordination with central and departmental administrators, the administrative and financial aspects of complex, awarded projects with broad impact. Provides broad management and oversight of financial and administrative aspects for assigned portfolios. Provides guidance to leadership on complex programmatic and financial matters. Maintains financial management and fiscal integrity for all contracts and grants according to agency-specific terms and conditions, the University of California policy and procedures, campus Internal Audit and the Business and Finance Financial Bulletins. Ensures compliance with the Federal Government OMB circulars for all awards. (25% time)

Reviews budget allocations for policy exceptions, conceives of and maintains chart of accounts or other data management tools, and related business processes. Reviews and reconciles ledger accounts. Participates in gathering data from the general ledger for the collection of information for UBIT, preparing summary schedules, and either answering questions from departments or coordinating getting answers. Responsible for ledger reconciliation, ensuring that backup documentation aligns with actual expenses and is accurately recorded. Also manages the reconciliation of other key areas, including personnel costs, effort reporting, and cost sharing. Processes journal entries, transfers, and corrections as necessary to maintain accurate financial records. (15% time)

(DR): Provides highly complex projections, analysis and recommendations. Analyzes personnel effort, spending patterns, and burn rates across multiple concurrent awards and projects, offering strategic recommendations to optimize resource allocation, ensure compliance, and address potential funding gaps or adjustments. (10% time)

Provides guidance and counsel on wide variety of highly complex research administration matters to principal investigators, senior departmental administrators and less experienced department staff. Leads education and outreach activities to facilitate connection between faculty and relevant programs/funding opportunities and promote research to external entities. Advises PI on agency reporting requirements including technical, financial and cost sharing reports to close out or renew awards. Works closely with PI throughout award periods and prior to closeout to ensure proper fund allocation and that all charges are accurately recorded before the project closeout. Advises and assists PI on rebudgeting, no-cost extensions, reductions in personnel support, etc., to ensure adherence to all policies, procedures and guidelines. (10% time)
Assists in support of audit as directed by senior staff. (5% time)
Prepares reviews and/or approves financial transactions. Independently gathers information as needed to perform financial analysis. (5% time)
Read/Comprehend: Constantly
Write: Constantly
Perform Calculations: Constantly
Communicate Orally: Constantly
Reason & Analyze: Constantly
Sit: Constantly
Stand: Occasionally
Walk: Occasionally

Full knowledge of Federal Acquisition Regulation, Code of Federal Regulations, sponsor-specific policies, intellectual property policy, conflict of interest requirements, publication rights, application of indirect cost rates and other complex concepts in research administration.
Maintains knowledge of and ability to interpret and apply sponsor, institutional and departmental policies. Knowledge of current compliance regulations in all areas of research administration.
Ability to manage high volume and complex transactions.
Ability to maintain independent judgment; strong organization and communication skills; and a customer service focus across broad and diverse subject areas.
Demonstrated advanced knowledge of generally accepted accounting, fiscal and reporting principles.
Ability to interpret policy for others.
Advanced knowledge of applicable compliance requirements related to use of human or animal subjects in research, financial conflict of interest, biosafety, etc.
Advances knowledge of effective grant funding processes, procedure and techniques.
Advanced ability to create and train grant writing and other communication skills in a variety of styles to ensure securing grant funding required.
Experience with all types of award mechanisms, including grants, contracts, subcontracts, cooperative agreements.
Ability to perform highly complex financial analysis and customized reporting.
Demonstrated advanced competence in the use of spreadsheet and database software in financial analysis, fiscal management and financial reports.
Extensive knowledge of program administration guidelines of Federal and non-Federal sponsors supporting research and educational activities, preferably in a university environment.
